newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Milling wheat down, maize futures up in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Milling wheat down, maize futures up in Hungary.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices continued to fall and maize prices rose on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) in moderate turnover, traders said on Wednesday.
"Improving weather and less pessimistic crop forecasts pushed wheat prices lower," said Janos Szolyka of Swap.
The two most traded milling wheat maturities, August and October dropped 360 and 330 forints per tonne, to end at 24,170 and 25,100 forints, respectively.
Feed wheat and feed barley prices also went down in the usual pattern of following milling wheat.
Maize prices went higher despite large rollover stocks in the absence of the selling side, traders said, but turnover remained low for all but the July maturity.
"Those who want to sell, will rather do that on the spot market," Szolyka said.
Total grains turnover was a below-average 541.2 million forints or 1,168 contracts, of which milling wheat accounted for 737 lots and maize for 285.
